w:r.w:t: TenderOS 2.1 - P2.1-FIX-A - Codex Re-audit
DCE Freshness Foundation
Mode: strict read-only
Executive Verdict
Verdict: PARTIALLY VALIDATED, BUT NOT SUFFICIENTLY RELIABLE AS A FOUNDATION. Remaining risk is P1.

The design introduced by FIX-A is conceptually sound: Dce.revision is a single monotonic freshness source, TenderAnalysisSummary.dceRevision is an additive nullable snapshot, and freshness is computed at read time as CURRENT, STALE or UNKNOWN without rewriting history.

The blocking issue is operational reliability. On the DCE mutation paths that matter most (ADD, REPLACE, DELETE, CATEGORY CHANGE), revision bumps are executed as cross-module best-effort side effects with catch-and-log behavior. If the increment fails after the semantic mutation succeeded, freshness can be reported incorrectly. That is not a cosmetic defect: it breaks the very trustworthiness of the new source of truth.

Files really belonging to FIX-A include at least: schema.prisma, migration 20261005091000_checkpoint_2_1_p2_1_fix_a_dce_freshness, analysis freshness types/use cases, DCE aggregate/repository/use cases, and frontend analysis freshness display types/components.
Prisma / Data Model
Dce.revision is really present as an integer semantic revision. Migration adds revision to dces as INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.
TenderAnalysisSummary.dceRevision is really present as a nullable additive column. Migration adds dce_revision to tender_analysis_summaries as nullable INTEGER with no default.
This is the correct historical stance: existing DCE rows become revision 1 baseline, historical summaries remain NULL and therefore UNKNOWN, not fake CURRENT.
Migration Audit
Migration file 20261005091000_checkpoint_2_1_p2_1_fix_a_dce_freshness is additive only.
No DROP, no rename, no destructive backfill, no false historical reconstruction found.
Historical preservation objective is respected at schema level.
Historical Preservation
No code found in FIX-A that deletes or rewrites historical DocumentVersion rows, historical Analysis rows, or historical TenderAnalysisSummary rows just to support freshness.
GetEffectiveTenderAnalysisSummary keeps base dceRevision/analysisFreshness from the base summary and layers user revisions on top without rewriting that base.
Append-only history is preserved. A COMPLETED analysis can indeed become STALE without being mutated or deleted.
Single Source of Truth Check
The new intended freshness SOT is clearly Dce.revision.
Freshness calculation is centralized in a pure function computeAnalysisFreshness(capturedDceRevision, currentDceRevision).
Read-time comparison is reused by GetTenderBusinessAnalysisUseCase and then carried through GetEffectiveTenderAnalysisSummaryUseCase.
I did not find a second competing freshness source such as updatedAt comparison, document timestamp comparison, fake stale booleans, or analysisVersion hijacking for this FIX-A foundation.
Conclusion on SOT shape: good.
Initial Baseline
Dce aggregate creates new DCEs with revision = 1. This matches the migration baseline and avoids invented prehistory.
Baseline semantics are coherent: first known state is revision 1, not 0 and not guessed from previous changes.
Freshness Read Path
Backend read path is coherent: business analysis latest summary is loaded, current DCE is resolved, and freshness is computed at read time.
UNKNOWN is returned whenever captured revision or current revision is unavailable, which is the right conservative behavior.
Frontend has aligned types and labels for CURRENT, STALE and UNKNOWN.
Where The Foundation Breaks
ADD path: import-dce-files.use-case increments DCE revision after successful document import, but wraps incrementRevision in catch-and-log best-effort behavior.
REPLACE path: replace-dce-document.use-case also increments revision in best-effort mode after AddDocumentVersionUseCase succeeds.
DELETE path: delete-dce-document.use-case increments revision in best-effort mode after DeleteDocumentUseCase succeeds.
CATEGORY CHANGE path: correct-dce-document-category.use-case increments revision in best-effort mode after effective category mutation.

The repository increment itself is technically strong: PrismaDceRepository.incrementRevision performs an atomic database increment using revision: { increment: 1 } under the composite key (id, organizationId). Integration tests explicitly cover concurrent increments.
The problem is not the increment primitive. The problem is when and how that primitive is invoked in the mutation flows.
Why This Is Still P1
If the semantic DCE mutation succeeds but incrementRevision fails and is swallowed, the current DCE revision remains too low.
From that moment, an older analysis summary can incorrectly compare equal to the stale DCE revision and appear CURRENT.
That is a false-negative on staleness, which defeats the purpose of FIX-A. The system would be declaring freshness where freshness is no longer known to be true.

Because FIX-B through FIX-F are expected to rely on this foundation, this is not acceptable technical debt for a source-of-truth layer. It would propagate incorrect trust decisions to later refresh gates and UI signals.
Non-Regression / Compatibility Notes

The new model is future-compatible with downstream consumers: analysis summary now carries dceRevision, effective summary preserves it, frontend displays freshness, and historical unknown handling is safe.
This means the conceptual interface is ready for future checkpoints. The reliability contract is what remains insufficient.
Findings
F1 - P1: Dce.revision propagation is not transactionally guaranteed on ADD/REPLACE/DELETE/CATEGORY CHANGE. Best-effort catch-and-log allows semantic DCE mutation without freshness source update.
F2 - P1: Because freshness is computed purely from Dce.revision versus captured dceRevision, a missed increment can misclassify stale analyses as CURRENT.
F3 - PASS: migration is additive-only and preserves history honestly.
F4 - PASS: historical summaries with NULL dceRevision resolve to UNKNOWN, not fabricated CURRENT.
F5 - PASS: increment primitive itself is atomic and concurrency-safe at repository level.
Foundation Decision
Is FIX-A sufficiently reliable to serve as the foundation for FIX-B to FIX-F?
Answer: No, not yet.
Architecture direction: valid.
Data model: valid.
Read-time freshness semantics: valid.
Operational reliability of the source-of-truth update: insufficient.
Final Status
P2.1-FIX-A should be considered ARCHITECTURALLY CORRECT BUT OPERATIONALLY NOT YET TRUSTWORTHY ENOUGH AS A FOUNDATION. The remaining best-effort propagation risk is still P1.
